name: phd-4plus1-double-count-used
description: A Ph.D. student from Notre Dame's 4+1 who HOLDS the MSCSE. Two senior-year courses counted toward both the bachelor's and the MSCSE ('both': excluded here, no course counts toward three degrees) and used up the Graduate School's six credits — "If 6 credits have double-counted to BS & MS, no more credits can double-count to BS & PhD later when the student pursues PhD" (through the DGS, 2026-09-22) — so a third senior-year course the bachelor's alone used ('bs') is over the allowance and counts nothing, and the row says why. A senior-year course only the MSCSE used ('mscse') counts in full (a master's-to-Ph.D. move in the same discipline), as does the fifth-year MSCSE coursework, without transfer approval and outside §5.2's cap. 2026-10-03: the “bs” course is counted on the Graduate School’s 2026-09-22 answer, which the Academic Code does not yet state, so it is provisional and the review request asks the DGS to confirm the rule — its line still says it is over the allowance. 2026-10-29 (credit-transfer review, C36): with the six spent no ruling can make it count, so it is no longer sent to the DGS and has no box; the approvals card waits only on the advisor.

CSE 60321: 3 credits not counted — beyond the allowance
